title: Modi and Nepal's Balen Shah to Flag Off Ayodhya–Janakpur Express on November 23
excerpt: The weekly direct service links Ayodhya Dham and Janakpur Dham over about 604 km with 10 intermediate stops; inaugural specials run November 23–25, with fares and the full regular timetable still to be published.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah are scheduled to jointly flag off the Ayodhya–Janakpur Express on Monday, November 23, 2026, during Shah's state visit to India.
  • The direct service links Ayodhya Dham in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur Dham in Nepal over about 604 km, with 10 intermediate stops across Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, the Ministry of Railways says.
  • The ministry says the regular service will run once a week: from Janakpur Dham on Saturdays and from Ayodhya Cantt on Mondays. Inaugural specials 04295 and 04296 run November 23–25.
  • Fares and the full regular timetable have not been published yet — check before planning a trip; customs procedures take place at Jaynagar on both sides of the border.
Launching November 23, 2026: the inaugural specials are scheduled and timed; the regular weekly pattern (Saturdays from Janakpur Dham, Mondays from Ayodhya Cantt) has been announced by the Ministry of Railways, but as of November 22 the full regular timetable and fares had not been published.

A direct train between Ayodhya and Janakpur — the two cities Hindus associate with Rama and Sita — begins running this week. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah are scheduled to jointly flag off the Ayodhya–Janakpur Express on Monday, November 23, one of the centrepieces of Shah's first state visit to India since taking office in March 2026, according to the Ministry of Railways announcement reported by Madhyamam.

The service covers around 604 kilometres. From Ayodhya Dham it runs through Mankapur, Basti and Gorakhpur in Uttar Pradesh, then Narkatiaganj, Raxaul, Sitamarhi, Shisho and Madhubani in Bihar, crossing into Nepal at Jaynagar before terminating at Janakpur Dham. "India and Nepal share centuries-old cultural, historical and social bonds, with religious traditions and cross-border community relationships forming an integral part of this partnership. The new train service will add another dimension to bilateral cooperation by using railway connectivity to bring communities closer," the ministry said.

The inaugural specials, timed

Indian Railways will run a special train for the inaugural journey, Jagran reported. Train 04295 leaves Ayodhya Dham at 12:30 p.m. on November 23 and reaches Janakpur Dham at 10:00 a.m. on November 24, with a customs halt at Jaynagar — 6:30–7:30 a.m. on the Indian side and 6:45–7:45 a.m. on the Nepalese side. The return special, 04296, leaves Janakpur Dham at 1:00 p.m. on November 24 and arrives at Ayodhya Dham at 8:10 a.m. on November 25. Jagran reports the regular services will carry the numbers 15595 (Ayodhya to Janakpur) and 15596 (return), while noting that Indian Railways has not yet formally confirmed the regular timetable.

Why this route matters

Ayodhya is revered as the birthplace of Rama and Janakpur as the home of Sita, and pilgrims have long travelled between the two by road or by changing trains at the border. A single direct train removes the change at Jaynagar for through passengers — customs checks still happen there, but travellers stay with the same service. The ministry said the improved connectivity is expected to make travel more convenient for pilgrims and tourists and to benefit hotels, shops and transport operators along the route. The flag-off also sits inside a wider visit: Shah's delegation-level talks with Modi on November 23 cover energy, connectivity and infrastructure, with several completed cross-border projects due to be inaugurated and new foundation stones laid during the visit.

Before planning your trip

  • Wait for the published regular timetable and fares — neither had been released as of November 22; the inaugural specials are not the regular service.
  • Build in the Jaynagar customs halt (about an hour on each side of the border) when planning onward connections.
  • Confirm which station you need: departures are listed from Ayodhya Dham for the inaugural special and Ayodhya Cantt for the regular weekly service.
  • Carry the identity documents you would normally need for India–Nepal border travel and verify requirements before you book.

For diaspora families planning a Ramayana-circuit trip — Ayodhya's Ram temple and Janakpur's Janaki Mandir in one journey — this is the first direct rail option between the two cities. The practical details that decide whether it works for a given itinerary, fares and the confirmed weekly timings, are the pieces still to come from Indian Railways.
